original_test_intent: Verify the management-I3C segment assigned to CPU1, including its documented target membership, device identities, address state and approved read responses, independently from CPU0 and from the unrelated E1S LED testcase.
original_method: A platform engineer defines how CPU1 maps to the BMC/OOB I3C controller and targets, freezes or approves the address-assignment state and read-only transaction set, and the agent captures per-target responses plus CPU1 and management health before and after the bounded check.
manual_activity: The platform engineer maps CPU1 to its I3C controller/segment and devices, distinguishes CPU0/shared targets, approves address handling and read transactions, and provides response and recovery criteria. No physical LED observation is part of this source row unless the Master is separately corrected.
required_inputs: BMC/OOB I3C controller and CPU1 segment topology
Shared-versus-CPU1-only target boundary and isolation semantics
Per-target PID, BCR, DCR and expected static/dynamic address
Current DAA state and explicit policy for any address-changing action
Vendor I3C utility/API and compatible BMC/CPLD/firmware versions
Approved CCC/private-read set and expected payload/status
CPU1 temperature, power, error and platform abort limits
safety_requirements: Never execute or credit the row-1904 LED procedure for this source key
Verify CPU1 association rather than assuming the second enumerated controller is CPU1
Do not credit shared targets twice across CPU0 and CPU1
Do not probe controllers, buses or addresses outside the approved map
Do not run DAA or broadcast/direct CCCs that can alter address/event/reset state without separate authorization
Exclude private writes and undocumented register access
Abort on address churn, shared-target ambiguity, bus error, CPU1/host/BMC instability, thermal or power excursion
Preserve first-fault evidence and do not automatically retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate the row/variant and CPU1 segment binding
Record controller and address state using the approved management interface
Collect only the named targets and permitted identity/status responses after confirmation
Compare each target against the CPU1-specific oracle and explicitly label shared devices
Correlate bus evidence with CPU1, BMC, SEL and thermal/power health
Perform no LED, cable, I/O-stimulus, write, reset or address-changing action
Leave the test verdict to the engineer
engineer_actions: Define CPU1 I3C ownership, topology and shared-device policy
Approve tool, address lifecycle, reads and expected outputs
Keep row 1904 E1S LED coverage independent
Review per-target evidence and decide the result

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The E1S BF3/CX8 LED observation has zero command or evidence overlap with CPU1 I3C. It cannot identify a controller or target and wrongly turns an automatable management-bus check into a physical-only task.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the project-approved BMC/OOB I3C interface to interrogate only CPU1's documented controller and target set, retaining PID/BCR/DCR, stable assigned addresses and allowlisted response data while explicitly separating shared targets from CPU0.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The literal I3C/CPU1 identity, code 00454, TBD fields and two-minute estimates are retained; E1S, BF3/CX8, LED colors and stimulus are not imported.

modernized_recommendation.status: CPU1 I3C MAP AND SAFE TRANSACTION CONTRACT REQUIRED
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Establish CPU1 segment ownership and pre-existing addresses, enumerate the approved target list without changing discovery state, collect identity and bounded status responses, reconcile CPU1-only/shared targets, then verify unchanged address and platform health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces the derived LED contamination with a source-aligned conditional I3C method while leaving the Master TBD fields intact.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Photos of E1S LEDs may validate row 1904 but prove nothing about CPU1 I3C. CPU0 results also do not prove CPU1 segment population or routing.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A mislabeled segment or state-changing CCC can disturb shared devices and obscure CPU association, so mapping and address-state controls are prerequisites.

project_override_considerations: If the project specification assigns CPU1 I3C to a host controller rather than BMC, the override must identify that controller and define equivalent target/address evidence. It cannot import E1S LED scope merely because the code is duplicated.
expected_evidence: Source key, variant/hash and exclusion of row-1904 LED coverage
CPU1-only versus shared target membership matrix
Complete bounded per-target reads with expected comparison
Explicit proof that CPU0 or shared responses were not double counted
CPU1 temperature/power/error plus BMC/SEL/bus health before and after

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row's Master fields consistently identify I3C CPU1 but omit implementation detail. E1S LED content exists only in the derived columns due to a duplicate-code match with a distinct row; it is an identity contamination, not a contradiction inside this source record.

blocked_analysis.analysis: I3C CPU1 has a definable conditional operation and evidence boundary under the Wistron rule. Platform-specific mapping and expectations must be supplied before execution, but ED-04 does not treat those normal inputs as an irreducible blocker.

review_improvement: Corrects the modality from manual LED inspection to conditional I3C automation, requires CPU1-versus-CPU0/shared-target attribution and prevents a duplicated code from merging two unrelated acceptance results.
independent_technical_reasoning: The strongest defect is not simply missing detail: a complete manual method from another row displaced this row's declared bus domain. I3C reachability is observable through a mapped controller and response oracle, so a human looking at an E1S LED is neither necessary nor sufficient. CPU1 must also be proven independently because a shared management device or CPU0 response could otherwise create a false positive for this segment.
